newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, INRO haunts market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, INRO haunts market.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was quiet by the midday break on Monday with the prospect of intervention by the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) casting a shadow over the market, dealers said.

"Some suppliers were holding back because they're afraid INRO might come in. The other dealers were also wary about INRO although most feel they will not come in at this time. The net result is a very quiet market," one dealer said.
The rubber trade has been waiting for INRO to intervene after its five-day indicator price slipped below the 183.00 cent level where it 'may-buy' to support rubber prices.
"Some people are worried that INRO may step in suddenly, but that seems unlikely for now," a dealer said.
Major consumers were also sitting on the sidelines, waiting for the picture in the market to clear up.
"The big boys have stepped back from the market. It would be foolish to play a hero in this market," a trader said.

At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 92.75 U.S. cents a kg from 93.50 cents. September RSS1 was indicated steady at 137.75 Singapore cents (95 U.S. cents) a kg. September TSR20 was indicated at 135.50 Singapore cents (94 U.S. cents) a kg from 136.00 cents. -(US$1 = S$1.44)- Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
